subject: Re: Evaluation acceleration / short extension & packaging options
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@novacorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Trial: small ask — add runway or alternative access?

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the run we've had with Redwood so far — the integration went smoother than expected. We're about halfway through our 30-day evaluation and seeing promising latency and quality for our use case, but two blockers have come up on our side that'd make it hard to finish a meaningful bake-off in the remaining time:

- Our QA cycle was delayed by a week due to a data-mapping issue (attached usage_snapshot.csv shows lower than expected token coverage).
- We need to validate concurrency under a small, controlled load pattern (peak bursts), which is hard to do from shared trial capacity.

Two asks — either would help:
1) A 14-day time extension on the trial so our QA team can finish scheduled tests, or
2) Short-term access to a dedicated evaluation pool (10 days) with slightly higher concurrency limits so we can validate burst behavior.

If extension is easier, a credit offer would work too — e.g., additional credits equivalent to ~$6k of usage to buy us time. If dedicated pool is feasible, what would that cost look like and how quickly can you provision?

We're keen to decide this week so engineering can schedule tests. Attached a short doc (MVP_requirements.docx) describing the scenarios we plan to run.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Applied ML
NovaCorp

Attachments: usage_snapshot.csv (csv), MVP_requirements.docx (docx)
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@novacorp.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@novacorp.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial: small ask — add runway or alternative access?

Hi Priya — appreciate the context and the attachments.

Short answer: we can do either, and we have two commonly used paths depending on speed and guarantees: 

Option A — 14-day trial extension with credit: we can add a 14-day timebox and top up the account with $6k of evaluation credits at a 20% applied discount (so you'd get $7.5k face-value usage). No changes to capacity, you stay on shared trial pool.

Option B — Dedicated evaluation pool (fastest for burst testing): we can provision a temporary dedicated pool for 10 calendar days. Typical workflow: 1) we reserve a small dedicated GPU allocation; 2) we apply a short-term rate (either flat daily or pre-bought credits); 3) after the 10 days we either convert the days used into committed capacity credits if you decide to proceed, or we tear down the pool. Pricing is normally $1,200/day for a modest dedicated slice (includes higher concurrency and priority routing). Converting to a committed seat within 30 days can earn you a credit back equal to 40% of the evaluation spend. Engineering lead David Kim is copied — David, can you confirm rough provisioning lead time (aiming for <72 hours) and any constraints on data ingestion for the dedicated pool?

A couple of notes: if you need SSO or private networking for the dedicated pool we'll need a short security checklist filled out (we can fast-track the SOC/attestation items for a temporary pool). Also, for accounting, Marissa (cc'ed on follow-ups) can create a short addendum instead of a full PO if that helps speed internal approvals.

If you prefer, we can do a hybrid: 7 days dedicated + 7 days time extension at a smaller credit top-up. Which path would you prefer?

Best,
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Olga — thanks for the quick options. After internal sync, we'd prefer Option B (dedicated evaluation pool) because burst behavior validation is the gating factor for our decision. A few quick clarifying questions: 

1) Can you confirm the $1,200/day estimate gets us the concurrency profile we need (our doc lists target burst: 80 concurrent requests with 3s tail latency under 95th percentile)?
2) Is there any one-time provisioning/setup fee?
3) If we convert to a committed purchase within 30 days, can the 40% conversion credit be applied against the first invoice?

One more ask: given we're on a tight timeline, would Redwood consider a one-time 20% discount on the dedicated pool days (i.e., $960/day) if we sign the evaluation addendum by EOD Friday? We'll cover provisioning and attach a short SOW. If you can do that, I'll get legal to sign the addendum quickly.

—Priya

Subject: Re: Trial: small ask — add runway or alternative access?

Priya — great, we can do the dedicated path and fast-track it. Confirming details below so finance/legal can move: 

- Scope: Dedicated evaluation pool, modest slice sized for targeted burst (aimed at your 80 concurrent request profile).
- Duration: 10 calendar days.
- Pricing: Standard $1,200/day -> total $12,000. We can apply a one-time 20% promotional discount if NovaCorp signs the evaluation addendum by EOD Friday, which brings total to $9,600. (This is a special promotional approval — Marissa, please confirm invoice flow.)
- Conversion: If NovaCorp converts to a committed plan within 30 days, Redwood will apply a credit equal to 40% of the actual evaluation spend (i.e., 40% of $9,600 = $3,840) against the first committed invoice.
- Provisioning lead time: David confirms engineering can provision the dedicated pool within 48 hours after addendum execution and customer SSO checklist completion.
- Setup fee: No one-time setup fee for this size; standard onboarding applies for SSO/networking if requested.

I've attached a short SOW and an order form to accelerate signatures: dedicated-access-order-form.pdf, SOW-eval-draft.docx. Tom — if you can have legal look at the addendum, we'll stand up capacity once signed.

Next steps:
1) Priya: confirm acceptance of the pricing above and whether you want Redwood to bill the $9,600 now or after the 10-day period.
2) Tom/legal: sign the short addendum (I'll send a DocuSign link once you confirm).
3) David/eng: once we have the signed addendum & SSO checklist, we provision (48-hour SLA).

If you'd like the hybrid 7+7 alternative instead let me know, but given your burst validation ask the dedicated 10 days is the cleanest signal.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
